subject: Mutual Action Plan: POC org setup, API keys & peering schedule
messages:
From: Claire Hsu <claire@orbhealth.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orbhealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC next steps — org / keys / peering

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the walkthrough this morning. We're excited to move the POC forward. Before we lock in a cutover window, procurement asked for a brief Mutual Action Plan so they can map internal signoffs. Can you share a single doc that lists the items we need to complete on our side (org setup, API keys, IP allowlist, and VPC peering), the recommended owners, and an estimated timeline?

Two quick clarifications from infra:
- For VPC peering, are you expecting us to provision a static IP for the peering tunnel or will Redwood initiate from your end?
- For API keys: can we use short-lived ephemeral keys for staging?

If you can send the MAP doc and a proposed schedule by EOD, procurement will start the review.

Best,
Claire
Product Ops — OrbHealth

Attachment: none in this message

From: rachel.kim@redwood.com
To: Claire Hsu <claire@orbhealth.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, procurement@orbhealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC next steps — org / keys / peering

Claire — thanks for the prompt. Attached is a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP-OrbHealth-v1-20250630.pdf) that breaks down:

1) Org bootstrap:
   - Action: Create "orbhealth-prod" and "orbhealth-staging" orgs in Redwood Console; invite two infra admins and two devs.
   - Owner (OrbHealth): infra-admin@orbhealth.com
   - Target: 2 business days after MAP sign-off

2) API keys & access:
   - Action: Redwood will generate scoped API keys for staging (ephemeral) and a long-lived key for dedicated evaluation.
   - Owner (Redwood): rachel.kim@redwood.com / marcus.lin@redwood.com
   - Note: Ephemeral keys are supported for staging; we'll provide a script to rotate them daily if you prefer.

3) IP allowlist / firewall:
   - Action: Add Redwood egress ranges to allowlist; file contains our current pool and a CIDR for peering verification.
   - Owner (OrbHealth): network-admin@orbhealth.com
   - Target: 48 hours before scheduled traffic test

4) VPC peering orchestration:
   - Action: Exchange peering credentials and test route advertisement. Redwood will initiate peering from our cloud account; OrbHealth must accept and verify routing.
   - Owner (joint): neha.kapoor@redwood.com / infra-admin@orbhealth.com
   - Target: Coordination call + test day (recommended 4-hour maintenance window)

I've put estimated dates in the attached MAP and an example 10-business-day close timeline. High level suggestion: org & keys in days 1–2, allowlist day 3, peering and test window days 5–7.

For procurement, I included the proposed DocuSign link for the MAP acceptance and a network diagram (orbhealth-network-diagram.png).

Next steps:
- Claire: confirm owners for the org and network items (I used infra-admin@orbhealth.com as a placeholder).
- Procurement: let us know any additional procurement artifacts you need and we'll loop Ben (ben.carter@redwood.com).

Thanks — I'll be available this afternoon for a short alignment call if helpful.

-Rachel
Rachel Kim
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0178

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com

Subject: Fwd: Mutual Action Plan: POC org setup, API keys & peering schedule

Quick internal coordination - forwarding Claire's acceptance and our proposed MAP.

Neha: can you confirm the peering flow below? My note in the MAP says Redwood will initiate the peering request from our AWS account (account id: 987654321). If OrbHealth wants to initiate from their side, we can flip it; just need a confirmed ARN and who will accept. Also call out whether we should request a static public IP for the peering verification (Claire's infra asked about that).

Ben: procurement will likely ask for our SOC2 and SFTP evidence for audit — please prep the short bundle and the DocuSign signature flow.

I propose we offer OrbHealth two options for peering:
- Option A (recommended): Redwood initiates peering; OrbHealth accepts. We provide routing test plan and a 4-hour test window.
- Option B: OrbHealth initiates; Redwood accepts. Slightly longer lead due to their change control.

If this looks good I'll put a calendar invite for a 30min peering alignment at 15:00 PT.

-Marcus
Senior Infrastructure PM | Redwood Inference

From: Claire Hsu <claire@orbhealth.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orbhealth.com, infra-admin@orbhealth.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: POC org setup, API keys & peering schedule

Rachel / Marcus — thanks for the detailed MAP and options. We've reviewed internally and confirm the following:

- Owners: infra-admin@orbhealth.com (network), devlead@orbhealth.com (org invites).
- Peering: OrbHealth prefers Option A (Redwood initiates). Please go ahead and send the peering request; we'll accept and run the routing test.
- Static IP: We'll allocate a short-lived public IP for verification, releases after tests.
- API keys: staging ephemeral keys will work for our engineers for the first two weeks; we'll request a long-lived key afterwards if the evaluation looks good.

Procurement — we're OK to start DocuSign for the MAP acceptance, please send over the final DocuSign link.

Let's use the 15:30 PT slot for the peering alignment call today; infra-admin will join.

Claire
